greet.text: Another one. The garrison sends a new face every spring. Sit if you're staying, stand if you're arresting me; I'm too old to care which. Zora. I keep the old fires out here, and nobody's licence says I can.

choices.text: What do you know about what's draining the valley?
(Scholar) You trained at the Collegium. I can tell from your hands.

again.text: Back again. The kettle's on. It's always on.

choices.text: What do you know about what's draining the valley?

drain.text: I know the shape of it. Someone's drawing the way the Collegium teaches you never to draw: through a vessel, from the living, slowly, so it doesn't kill at once. That takes training. Somebody learned at a college, and then left it. Or didn't leave.

scholar.text: She turns her hands over and laughs. "Thirty years ago. They wanted me to sign the Accords; I wanted to keep my fire. Watch who you trust in those halls, child. Not everyone in a robe is a scholar."

arrest.text: Then do it. I'll walk. I won't fight a child of the garrison; it never ends well for anyone. But you could also not.

choices.text: Come with me. You'll get a fair hearing in Riverwatch.
Go. Get deeper into the forest before they send someone else.
Teach me something, and I'll say I never found you.

arrested.text: "Fair," she says, as if tasting the word. She banks her fire, takes her stick, and walks ahead of you without being asked. At the edge of the trees she says: "Tell your scout the goats were never me."

warned.text: She looks at you for a long moment. "Then the forest owes you one, and so do I." By the time you've turned round, the fire's out and she's gone.

taught_now.text: A bargain! The garrison would be horrified. Here: frost, not fire. Fire is easy and everyone learns it; cold is patient. Read it somewhere quiet.

taught.text: Practising? Badly, I hope; that's how it starts. Mind you tell your scout you never found me.

choices.text: What do you know about what's draining the valley?
(Scholar) You trained at the Collegium. I can tell from your hands.

sees_stain.text: She takes your wrist before you can stop her and turns it to the firelight. "Drawn. Not much, yet." She lets go. "It'll make your spells sing and your cuts slow to close, and it wants more of itself. The shrine on the north road can take it back out of you, a night at a time, if anyone's lit it."

sees_stain_how.text: Because I was offered it, thirty years ago, in a quiet room at the Collegium. I said no. Some of the people in that room didn't.
